messages.content: You can call send_email to compose and send messages. Always confirm critical fields before sending.
Send an email to alice@example.com thanking her for yesterday's meeting and proposing a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM.

function.name: send_email
function.description: Compose and send an email message.

message.content:
<think>The user wants to send an email to alice@example.com thanking her for yesterday's meeting and proposing a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM. I have the send_email tool available. Let me compose and send this email.

I need to:
1. Set the recipient to alice@example.com
2. Set the subject (something like "Follow-up from our meeting" or "Thank you for yesterday's meeting")
3. Set the body with a thank you message and the proposed Friday 3 PM follow-up call

Let me send this email.
</think>

function.name: send_email
function.arguments:
{"to": ["alice@example.com"], "subject": "Follow-up from Yesterday's Meeting", "body": "Hi Alice,

Thank you for meeting with me yesterday. I really appreciated the time we spent together and found our conversation very valuable.

I would love to continue our discussion. Would you be available for a follow-up call this Friday at 3 PM? Please let me know if that time works for you or if you would prefer a different slot.

Looking forward to hearing from you.

Best regards"}
